answer: The ledger treats each agent as a node perched on a karst‑etched ledge, and every new identity must present a signed lantern‑token that proves co‑ownership of a shared vault or payment source with an existing node. A verifier checks the cryptographic link; if the token matches a previously recorded vault, the node is merged into the existing entity and its voting weight is capped. An attacker therefore must acquire a full vault or duplicate a live payment stream for every fake node, raising the cost to the linear sum of real‑world resources rather than a negligible hash.
